objects.description: Opaque ZeroMQ message container with fixed-size, alignment-sensitive storage. Must be initialized and closed with zmq_msg_* APIs. Data and metadata are managed by the library.
Callback type invoked by the library to free application-owned buffers attached to a zmq_msg_t. The hint pointer is passed back verbatim.
Integral type that abstracts the OS socket/file descriptor used by ZeroMQ for polling. Width varies by platform.
Poll item used with deprecated zmq_poll/zmq_ppoll. It can represent either a ZeroMQ socket (socket non-null) or a raw OS fd (fd set).
Callback signature for timer events scheduled via the zmq_timers_* API. Receives the timer id and user argument.
Thread entry-point callback type used by zmq_threadstart/zmq_threadclose helpers.

functions.name: zmq_errno
functions.description: Returns the current ZeroMQ-specific errno value. Use this after an API call fails to retrieve the error code in a CRT-independent way (especially on Windows).
requirements: Call only to read error code after a preceding ZeroMQ API call indicates failure.

functions.name: zmq_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string for the given system or ZeroMQ error number.
requirements: errnum_ should be a valid errno or ZeroMQ error code (e.g., EFSM, ETERM).
The returned string must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: zmq_version
functions.description: Writes the ZeroMQ library version (major, minor, patch) to the provided pointers for runtime version detection.
requirements: major_, minor_, and patch_ must be non-NULL pointers to int.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_new
functions.description: Creates a new ZeroMQ context and returns an opaque handle. This is the starting point for creating sockets.
requirements: Must be called before socket creation.
Returned context must be terminated with zmq_ctx_term or zmq_ctx_shutdown + zmq_ctx_term.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_term
functions.description: Terminates a ZeroMQ context, closing any remaining sockets and freeing resources. Blocks until all sockets are closed.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context pointer returned by zmq_ctx_new or zmq_init.
Must not be called concurrently with other operations on the same context.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_shutdown
functions.description: Initiates shutdown of a ZeroMQ context, causing blocking calls on sockets to return with ETERM. Non-blocking; follow with zmq_ctx_term to complete termination.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context pointer returned by zmq_ctx_new or zmq_init.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_set
functions.signature: int zmq_ctx_set(void *context_, int option_, int optval_);
functions.description: Sets a context-level option (e.g., ZMQ_IO_THREADS, ZMQ_MAX_SOCKETS).
requirements: context_ must be a valid context.
option_ must be one of the defined context options (e.g., ZMQ_IO_THREADS, ZMQ_MAX_SOCKETS, etc.).
optval_ must satisfy the specific option's constraints (e.g., non-negative where applicable).

functions.name: zmq_ctx_get
functions.description: Gets a context-level option value.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context.
option_ must be one of the defined context options.

functions.name: zmq_init
functions.description: Legacy API. Creates a ZeroMQ context specifying the number of I/O threads. Prefer zmq_ctx_new and zmq_ctx_set.
requirements: io_threads_ should be a non-negative integer.
Returned context must be terminated with zmq_term or zmq_ctx_term.

functions.name: zmq_term
functions.description: Legacy API. Terminates a ZeroMQ context created by zmq_init (or zmq_ctx_new). Equivalent to zmq_ctx_term.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_destroy
functions.description: Legacy alias for zmq_ctx_term. Terminates a context.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context pointer.

functions.name: zmq_msg_init
functions.description: Initializes an empty ZeroMQ message.
requirements: msg_ must be a non-NULL pointer to zmq_msg_t.
The zmq_msg_t object should be allocated at an address aligned to a pointer-size boundary (per header note) to avoid SIGBUS on some architectures.
Must be closed with zmq_msg_close when no longer needed.

functions.name: zmq_msg_init_size
functions.description: Initializes a message with a given size allocating its content buffer.
requirements: msg_ must be non-NULL and aligned as per zmq_msg_t note.
size_ is the number of bytes to allocate; must fit in memory.
Close with zmq_msg_close after use.

functions.name: zmq_msg_init_data
functions.signature: int zmq_msg_init_data(zmq_msg_t *msg_, void *data_, size_t size_, zmq_free_fn *ffn_, void *hint_);
functions.description: Initializes a message that uses an existing data buffer and registers a deallocation callback invoked when the message is closed.
requirements: msg_ must be non-NULL and aligned as per zmq_msg_t note.
data_ points to a buffer of at least size_ bytes and must remain valid until the message is closed.
ffn_ is a callback of type void(*)(void*,void*) that will be called with (data_, hint_) when the message is deallocated; it may be NULL depending on library behavior (unknown).
Close with zmq_msg_close to trigger the free callback.

functions.name: zmq_msg_send
functions.description: Sends a message over a ZeroMQ socket. On success returns number of bytes sent and consumes/invalidates the content of msg_.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t; ownership semantics follow ZeroMQ (message content is consumed).
s_ must be a valid ZeroMQ socket created by zmq_socket.
flags_ must be 0 or a combination including ZMQ_DONTWAIT and/or ZMQ_SNDMORE.
Do not access msg_ content after successful send unless reinitialized.

functions.name: zmq_msg_recv
functions.description: Receives a message from a ZeroMQ socket into msg_. Returns number of bytes received.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t, typically empty before receive.
s_ must be a valid ZeroMQ socket.
flags_ must be 0 or ZMQ_DONTWAIT.
Close msg_ with zmq_msg_close when done.

functions.name: zmq_msg_close
functions.description: Closes a message, releasing its resources and invoking any registered free callback.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
Do not use msg_ after closing unless reinitialized.

functions.name: zmq_msg_move
functions.description: Moves the content from src_ to dest_, leaving src_ empty. Used for zero-copy transfers.
requirements: dest_ and src_ must be initialized zmq_msg_t.
After move, src_ should not be used without reinitialization.
dest_ must be closed when done.

functions.name: zmq_msg_copy
functions.description: Copies the content from src_ to dest_.
requirements: dest_ and src_ must be initialized zmq_msg_t.
dest_ must be closed when done.

functions.name: zmq_msg_data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the message data buffer for read/write access.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t with data (may be zero-sized).
The returned pointer remains valid while the message is not closed or modified by other operations.

functions.name: zmq_msg_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the message data.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.

functions.name: zmq_msg_more
functions.description: Returns non-zero if there are more message parts to receive (multipart message indicator).
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t received from a socket.

functions.name: zmq_msg_get
functions.description: Gets a property of the message (e.g., more flag, shared, etc.).
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
property_ must be a supported message property constant.

functions.name: zmq_msg_set
functions.signature: int zmq_msg_set(zmq_msg_t *msg_, int property_, int optval_);
functions.description: Sets a property on the message if supported.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
property_ must be a supported message property constant.
optval_ must satisfy the property-specific constraints.

functions.name: zmq_msg_gets
functions.description: Gets a string property from a message by name, e.g., metadata entries. Returns a pointer to an internal string.
requirements: msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
property_ must be a valid property name string.
Returned string must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: zmq_socket
functions.description: Creates a ZeroMQ socket of the specified type (e.g., ZMQ_REQ, ZMQ_SUB) within the given context.
requirements: context_ must be a valid context.
type_ must be one of the defined ZMQ socket types.

functions.name: zmq_close
functions.description: Closes a ZeroMQ socket and releases its resources.
requirements: s_ must be a valid ZeroMQ socket handle created by zmq_socket.
Do not use the socket after closing.

functions.name: zmq_setsockopt
functions.signature: int zmq_setsockopt(void *s_, int option_, const void *optval_, size_t optvallen_);
functions.description: Sets a socket option on a ZeroMQ socket.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
option_ must be a defined socket option constant.
optval_ must point to a buffer containing the option value of the correct type and length.
optvallen_ must be the size in bytes of the option value.

functions.name: zmq_getsockopt
functions.signature: int zmq_getsockopt(void *s_, int option_, void *optval_, size_t *optvallen_);
functions.description: Gets a socket option from a ZeroMQ socket.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
option_ must be a defined socket option constant.
optval_ must point to a buffer large enough to receive the value.
optvallen_ must be a non-NULL pointer to a size_t containing the buffer size on input and updated with actual size on output.

functions.name: zmq_bind
functions.description: Binds a socket to an endpoint address string (e.g., tcp://*:5555).
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket compatible with binding.
addr_ must be a non-NULL, valid ZeroMQ endpoint string.

functions.name: zmq_connect
functions.description: Connects a socket to an endpoint address string.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
addr_ must be a non-NULL, valid ZeroMQ endpoint string.

functions.name: zmq_unbind
functions.description: Unbinds a socket from a previously bound endpoint.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
addr_ must match a previously bound endpoint string.

functions.name: zmq_disconnect
functions.description: Disconnects a socket from a previously connected endpoint.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
addr_ must match a previously connected endpoint string.

functions.name: zmq_send
functions.signature: int zmq_send(void *s_, const void *buf_, size_t len_, int flags_);
functions.description: Sends a frame from a raw buffer on a ZeroMQ socket.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
buf_ must point to at least len_ bytes (buffer remains owned by caller).
len_ is the number of bytes to send.
flags_ must be 0 or combination including ZMQ_DONTWAIT and/or ZMQ_SNDMORE.

functions.name: zmq_send_const
functions.signature: int zmq_send_const(void *s_, const void *buf_, size_t len_, int flags_);
functions.description: Sends a frame from a constant (immutable/static) buffer on a ZeroMQ socket, possibly avoiding copies.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
buf_ must point to at least len_ bytes that remain valid for the duration of the send.
flags_ must be 0 or combination including ZMQ_DONTWAIT and/or ZMQ_SNDMORE.

functions.name: zmq_recv
functions.signature: int zmq_recv(void *s_, void *buf_, size_t len_, int flags_);
functions.description: Receives a frame into a caller-supplied buffer. Returns number of bytes received.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
buf_ must point to a buffer of at least len_ bytes.
flags_ must be 0 or ZMQ_DONTWAIT.

functions.name: zmq_socket_monitor
functions.signature: int zmq_socket_monitor(void *s_, const char *addr_, int events_);
functions.description: Enables socket monitoring by having the socket publish events on an inproc endpoint.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
addr_ must be a valid endpoint (typically inproc://...).
events_ is a bitmask of ZMQ_EVENT_* constants.

functions.name: zmq_poll
functions.signature: int zmq_poll(zmq_pollitem_t *items_, int nitems_, long timeout_);
functions.description: Deprecated I/O multiplexing. Polls a set of sockets or FDs for events.
requirements: items_ must point to an array of at least nitems_ elements.
nitems_ must be >= 0.
timeout_ is in milliseconds; -1 to wait forever, 0 for non-blocking.

functions.name: zmq_proxy
functions.description: Runs a built-in message proxy device forwarding between frontend and backend sockets, optionally capturing traffic.
requirements: frontend_ and backend_ must be valid sockets of appropriate types.
capture_ may be NULL or a valid socket for duplication/capture.
This function typically runs until interrupted; call in a dedicated thread or process.

functions.name: zmq_proxy_steerable
functions.description: Like zmq_proxy but adds a control socket to steer/interrupt the proxy via control messages.
requirements: frontend_ and backend_ must be valid sockets.
capture_ may be NULL or a valid socket.
control_ must be a valid socket used to send control commands (format unspecified here).

functions.name: zmq_has
functions.description: Probes whether a given capability string is supported by the library at runtime (e.g., "curve"). Returns non-zero if supported.
requirements: capability_ must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: zmq_device
functions.description: Deprecated method. Runs a predefined device (e.g., streamer, queue, forwarder). Replaced by zmq_proxy.
requirements: type_ should be one of deprecated device types (ZMQ_STREAMER, ZMQ_FORWARDER, ZMQ_QUEUE).
frontend_ and backend_ must be valid sockets.

functions.name: zmq_sendmsg
functions.description: Deprecated alias for zmq_msg_send. Sends an initialized message on a socket.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
flags_ must be 0 or combination including ZMQ_DONTWAIT and/or ZMQ_SNDMORE.

functions.name: zmq_recvmsg
functions.description: Deprecated alias for zmq_msg_recv. Receives a message into msg_.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
msg_ must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
flags_ must be 0 or ZMQ_DONTWAIT.

functions.name: zmq_sendiov
functions.signature: int zmq_sendiov(void *s_, struct iovec *iov_, size_t count_, int flags_);
functions.description: Deprecated method. Sends multiple buffers (iovecs) as a single multipart message.
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
iov_ must point to an array of at least count_ struct iovec entries.
count_ is the number of iovecs.
flags_ must be 0 or include ZMQ_DONTWAIT; use ZMQ_SNDMORE semantics through iovecs and socket type (details unspecified here).

functions.name: zmq_recviov
functions.signature: int zmq_recviov(void *s_, struct iovec *iov_, size_t *count_, int flags_);
functions.description: Deprecated method. Receives a message into multiple buffers (iovecs).
requirements: s_ must be a valid socket.
iov_ must point to an array that can hold at least *count_ iovecs.
count_ must be a non-NULL pointer; on input provides max elements, on output updated with number filled.
flags_ must be 0 or ZMQ_DONTWAIT.

functions.name: zmq_z85_encode
functions.description: Encodes binary data into Z85 (ZeroMQ Base-85) textual representation. Returns dest_.
requirements: dest_ must point to a buffer large enough to hold the encoded output including terminator if needed (size_ must be a multiple appropriate for Z85, typically multiple of 4 bytes; exact constraint not specified here).
data_ must point to size_ bytes of input data.
size_ must satisfy Z85 input-size constraints (unknown exact rule here).

functions.name: zmq_z85_decode
functions.description: Decodes a Z85-encoded string into binary data. Returns dest_.
requirements: dest_ must point to a buffer large enough to hold the decoded bytes.
string_ must be a valid, properly sized Z85 string (length must satisfy Z85 constraints; exact rule not specified here).

functions.name: zmq_curve_keypair
functions.description: Generates a CurveZMQ (libsodium) public/secret key pair encoded in Z85. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: z85_public_key_ and z85_secret_key_ must point to writable buffers large enough for Z85-encoded keys plus terminators.

functions.name: zmq_curve_public
functions.description: Derives the Z85-encoded public key from a Z85-encoded secret key. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: z85_public_key_ must be a writable buffer large enough for the encoded public key.
z85_secret_key_ must be a valid Z85-encoded Curve secret key string.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_new
functions.description: Creates a new atomic counter object and returns an opaque handle.
requirements: Destroy with zmq_atomic_counter_destroy when done.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_set
functions.description: Sets the counter to a specific value.
requirements: counter_ must be a valid atomic counter handle created by zmq_atomic_counter_new.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_inc
functions.description: Atomically increments the counter and returns the incremented value (or new value).
requirements: counter_ must be a valid atomic counter handle.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_dec
functions.description: Atomically decrements the counter and returns the decremented value (or new value).
requirements: counter_ must be a valid atomic counter handle.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_value
functions.description: Returns the current value of the atomic counter.
requirements: counter_ must be a valid atomic counter handle.

functions.name: zmq_atomic_counter_destroy
functions.description: Destroys an atomic counter and sets the handle pointer to NULL.
requirements: counter_p_ must be a non-NULL pointer to a counter handle created by zmq_atomic_counter_new.
*counter_p_ must be a valid handle or NULL.

functions.name: zmq_timers_new
functions.description: Creates a timers scheduler object and returns an opaque handle.
requirements: Destroy with zmq_timers_destroy when done.

functions.name: zmq_timers_destroy
functions.description: Destroys a timers scheduler and sets the handle pointer to NULL.
requirements: timers_p must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid timers handle or NULL.

functions.name: zmq_timers_add
functions.signature: int zmq_timers_add(void *timers, size_t interval, zmq_timer_fn handler, void *arg);
functions.description: Adds a periodic timer with the given interval in milliseconds and a callback handler. Returns a timer id.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.
interval is in milliseconds and should be > 0 for a periodic timer (exact constraints not specified).
handler must be a non-NULL function pointer of type void(int, void*).

functions.name: zmq_timers_cancel
functions.description: Cancels a previously added timer by id.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.
timer_id must be a valid id returned by zmq_timers_add.

functions.name: zmq_timers_set_interval
functions.signature: int zmq_timers_set_interval(void *timers, int timer_id, size_t interval);
functions.description: Changes the interval of an existing timer.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.
timer_id must be a valid timer id.
interval is in milliseconds (must be a valid value; exact constraints not specified).

functions.name: zmq_timers_reset
functions.description: Resets a timer's next firing time to now + its interval.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.
timer_id must be a valid timer id.

functions.name: zmq_timers_timeout
functions.description: Returns the time in milliseconds until the next timer expiration, or -1 if none.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.

functions.name: zmq_timers_execute
functions.description: Executes due timers' callbacks. Should be called periodically based on zmq_timers_timeout.
requirements: timers must be a valid timers scheduler handle.

functions.name: zmq_stopwatch_start
functions.description: Starts a high-resolution stopwatch and returns a handle.
requirements: Use with zmq_stopwatch_intermediate and zmq_stopwatch_stop.
These helpers are not documented by man pages; use at your own risk.

functions.name: zmq_stopwatch_intermediate
functions.description: Returns microseconds elapsed since the stopwatch was started without stopping it.
requirements: watch_ must be a valid stopwatch handle returned by zmq_stopwatch_start.

functions.name: zmq_stopwatch_stop
functions.description: Stops the stopwatch, returns microseconds elapsed, and deallocates the handle.
requirements: watch_ must be a valid stopwatch handle returned by zmq_stopwatch_start.
Do not reuse watch_ after this call.

functions.name: zmq_sleep
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread for the specified number of seconds.
requirements: seconds_ should be >= 0 (typical expectation; exact constraints not specified).

functions.name: zmq_threadstart
functions.description: Starts a new thread executing func_(arg_) and returns a thread handle.
requirements: func_ must be a non-NULL function pointer of type void(void*).
Close with zmq_threadclose when the thread has completed (or to join/cleanup).

functions.name: zmq_threadclose
functions.description: Waits for the specified thread to complete and frees resources.
requirements: thread_ must be a handle returned by zmq_threadstart.
The target thread should cooperate to exit for timely completion.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_set_ext
functions.signature: int zmq_ctx_set_ext(void *context_, int option_, const void *optval_, size_t optvallen_);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Extended context option setter that accepts typed buffers.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API at compile time/link time.
context_ must be a valid context.
option_ must be a supported draft context option (e.g., ZMQ_ZERO_COPY_RECV).
optval_ points to the option value; optvallen_ is its size in bytes.

functions.name: zmq_ctx_get_ext
functions.signature: int zmq_ctx_get_ext(void *context_, int option_, void *optval_, size_t *optvallen_);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Extended context option getter that writes into a caller-provided buffer.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
context_ must be a valid context.
option_ must be a supported draft context option.
optval_ must point to a buffer; *optvallen_ must contain buffer size on input and is set to actual size on output.

functions.name: zmq_join
functions.description: DRAFT API. Joins a RADIO/DISH or group-capable socket to a group name.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
s must be a valid socket supporting groups (e.g., ZMQ_DISH/ZMQ_RADIO).
group must be a non-NULL string up to ZMQ_GROUP_MAX_LENGTH.

functions.name: zmq_leave
functions.description: DRAFT API. Leaves a previously joined group.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
s must be a valid group-capable socket.
group must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: zmq_connect_peer
functions.description: DRAFT API. Connects a peer-to-peer capable socket to an address and returns a routing id (peer id).
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
s_ must be a valid peer-capable socket.
addr_ must be a valid endpoint string.

functions.name: zmq_msg_set_routing_id
functions.description: DRAFT API. Sets the routing id on a message for ROUTER/DEALER style routing.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
msg must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.

functions.name: zmq_msg_routing_id
functions.description: DRAFT API. Gets the routing id from a message.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
msg must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.

functions.name: zmq_msg_set_group
functions.description: DRAFT API. Sets the group name on a message (RADIO/DISH).
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
msg must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
group must be a non-NULL string.

functions.name: zmq_msg_group
functions.description: DRAFT API. Retrieves the group name from a message.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
msg must be an initialized zmq_msg_t.
Returned string must not be modified or freed by the caller.

functions.name: zmq_msg_init_buffer
functions.signature: int zmq_msg_init_buffer(zmq_msg_t *msg_, const void *buf_, size_t size_);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Initializes a message by copying from a caller-provided buffer.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
msg_ must be non-NULL and aligned as per zmq_msg_t note.
buf_ must point to at least size_ bytes.

functions.name: zmq_poller_new
functions.description: DRAFT API. Creates a poller object that can wait on sockets and FDs.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
Destroy with zmq_poller_destroy.

functions.name: zmq_poller_destroy
functions.description: DRAFT API. Destroys a poller object and sets the handle pointer to NULL.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller_p must be a non-NULL pointer to a poller handle or NULL.

functions.name: zmq_poller_size
functions.description: DRAFT API. Returns the number of items registered in the poller.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be a valid poller handle.

functions.name: zmq_poller_add
functions.signature: int zmq_poller_add(void *poller, void *socket, void *user_data, short events);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Adds a ZeroMQ socket to the poller with associated user data and event mask.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be a valid poller handle.
socket must be a valid ZeroMQ socket.
events is a bitmask of ZMQ_POLLIN/ZMQ_POLLOUT/etc.

functions.name: zmq_poller_modify
functions.description: DRAFT API. Modifies the event mask for a registered socket.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
socket must have been previously added to this poller.
events is a bitmask of events.

functions.name: zmq_poller_remove
functions.description: DRAFT API. Removes a socket from the poller.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
socket must have been previously added.

functions.name: zmq_poller_wait
functions.description: DRAFT API. Waits for one event and writes it to event. Returns number of events (0 on timeout).
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
event must point to a valid zmq_poller_event_t struct.
timeout is in milliseconds; -1 to wait forever, 0 for non-blocking.

functions.name: zmq_poller_wait_all
functions.signature: int zmq_poller_wait_all(void *poller, zmq_poller_event_t *events, int n_events, long timeout);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Waits for up to n_events events and writes them into the events array.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
events must point to an array of at least n_events entries.
n_events must be > 0.
timeout is in milliseconds; -1 to wait forever, 0 for non-blocking.

functions.name: zmq_poller_fd
functions.description: DRAFT API. Retrieves an OS-level file descriptor for integration with external poll loops.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
fd must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the descriptor.

functions.name: zmq_poller_add_fd
functions.signature: int zmq_poller_add_fd(void *poller, zmq_fd_t fd, void *user_data, short events);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Adds a raw file descriptor to the poller with user data and event mask.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
fd must be a valid OS file descriptor/handle.
events is a bitmask of events.

functions.name: zmq_poller_modify_fd
functions.signature: int zmq_poller_modify_fd(void *poller, zmq_fd_t fd, short events);
functions.description: DRAFT API. Modifies the event mask for a registered FD.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.
poller must be valid.
fd must have been previously added.
events is a bitmask of events.

functions.name: zmq_poller_remove_fd
functions.description: DRAFT API. Removes a raw FD from the poller.
requirements: Requires ZMQ_BUILD_DRAFT_API.

data_types.description: A general-purpose C-style string (UTF-8 or arbitrary bytes treated as text) used as a property name or tag. No specific format constraints beyond being non-empty and NUL-terminated when passed to C APIs.

A ZeroMQ endpoint URI such as inproc://name, tcp://host:port, ipc://path. In these stubs specifically, an inproc endpoint is constructed (e.g., inproc://<tag>). Must be a valid non-empty endpoint string.
An unrestricted byte buffer whose contents are treated as opaque data payload; may include any bytes including NUL. Used for sending message frames.
A textual capability identifier for ZeroMQ features (e.g., "curve"). Any non-empty string may be queried; recognized values return non-zero.
Text encoded using ZeroMQ's Z85 (Base-85) alphabet representing binary data. Length must be a multiple of 5 characters; decodes to 4 bytes per 5 chars.
A 40-character Z85 string representing a CurveZMQ (Curve25519) secret key, followed by a NUL terminator when passed to C APIs.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for:
# - zmq_msg_gets: expects a non-empty property name string
# - zmq_socket_monitor: expects an inproc endpoint tag segment to be concatenated
#   into "inproc://mon-<tag>"; also reads an unsigned int selector and possibly
#   another string. FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) draw from the same
#   input buffer sequentially.
#
# We therefore craft a bytes buffer that contains, in order:
# 1) A 4-byte unsigned int (little-endian) selector with mixed parity to exercise
#    both enable/disable monitoring code paths.
# 2) A length-prefixed string corpus that FUZZ_PARAM_STR can parse repeatedly.
#    Typical fuzz harnesses extract strings by scanning for NUL or by size-prefix.
#    To stay broadly compatible, we provide multiple NUL-terminated strings back-to-back.
#    - First string set: properties for zmq_msg_gets (various known/interesting names)
#    - Second string set: tags for zmq_socket_monitor inproc address (up to 16 chars)
#
# We ensure the buffer is under 4096 bytes and contains only valid C-strings.

KNOWN_MSG_PROPERTIES = [
    # Commonly implemented properties in libzmq for zmq_msg_gets
    "Peer-Address", "Socket-Type", "User-Id", "Routing-Id", "Group",
    "Identity", "Mechanism", "Subscription", "Content-Type", "Metadata",
    # Edge/unusual
    "more", "MORE", "shared", "SHARED", "",  # empty will be filtered earlier by stub
]

# Some interesting tags to build inproc endpoints for monitoring
INTERESTING_TAGS = [
    "a", "mon", "X", "abc123", "tag-with-dash", "under_score",
    "dots.tag", "UNICODE-µ", "空间", "longtag0123456789", "END",
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_+."


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _cstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Convert to UTF-8 C-string (NUL terminated)
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore") + b"\x00"


def _build_strings_block(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    # Property names: choose a mix of known and random
    prop_count = r.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(prop_count):
        if r.random() < 0.7:
            # pick known non-empty; filter out empty here
            cand = r.choice([p for p in KNOWN_MSG_PROPERTIES if p])
        else:
            cand = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 24)
        parts.append(_cstr(cand))

    # Tags for inproc monitor address: up to 16 characters used by stub
    tag_count = r.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(tag_count):
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            tag = r.choice(INTERESTING_TAGS)
        else:
            tag = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 24)
        # Provide both a short and a longer version sometimes
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            tag = tag[:16]
        parts.append(_cstr(tag))

    # Guarantee at least one strictly non-empty string
    if not parts:
        parts.append(_cstr("prop"))

    return b"".join(parts)


def _build_selector(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create a selector with random parity to toggle the two paths.
    # Sometimes force even (enable), sometimes odd (disable).
    mode = r.random()
    if mode < 0.34:
        sel = r.getrandbits(32) & ~1  # even => enable
    elif mode < 0.67:
        sel = (r.getrandbits(32) | 1)  # odd => disable
    else:
        sel = r.getrandbits(32)  # random
    return sel.to_bytes(4, byteorder="little", signed=False)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    buf = bytearray()

    # 1) Selector for zmq_socket_monitor branch
    buf += _build_selector(r)

    # 2) NUL-terminated strings block used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    strings_blob = _build_strings_block(r)

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    max_extra = 4096 - len(buf)
    if len(strings_blob) > max_extra:
        strings_blob = strings_blob[:max_extra]
        # ensure last byte is NUL to terminate last string
        if not strings_blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
            if len(strings_blob) > 0:
                strings_blob = strings_blob[:-1] + b"\x00"
            else:
                strings_blob = b"\x00"

    buf += strings_blob

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for ZeroMQ endpoint string inputs used by stubs constructing inproc://<name>
# The fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and ensure it is non-empty; they then
# build endpoint = "inproc://" + name.substr(0, 32).
# We therefore provide non-empty strings with interesting characteristics within 32 chars
# to exercise parsing and name handling, while remaining valid for inproc transport.

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096

INPROC_SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:@+%"

def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def _weighted(r: random.Random, items):
    total = sum(w for w, _ in items)
    x = r.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for w, v in items:
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return v
    return items[-1][1]

def _make_inproc_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Length 1..32 (stubs trim to 32). Bias towards edge lengths.
    length = _weighted(r, [
        (2, 1), (2, 2), (2, 3), (2, 4),
        (4, 8), (4, 16), (4, 31), (6, 32)
    ])

    strategies = []
    # Simple alnum
    def s_simple():
        return ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(length))
    strategies.append(s_simple)

    # Mixed case with separators
    def s_mixed():
        parts = []
        while len(''.join(parts)) < length:
            chunk_len = r.randint(1, max(1, min(6, length - len(''.join(parts)))))
            chunk = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(chunk_len))
            parts.append(chunk)
            if len(''.join(parts)) < length:
                parts.append(r.choice(['-', '_', '.', ':', '+']))
        s = ''.join(parts)[:length]
        return s
    strategies.append(s_mixed)

    # Percent-encoded style content
    def s_pct():
        out = []
        while len(''.join(out)) < length:
            if r.random() < 0.3 and len(''.join(out)) <= length - 3:
                b = r.randrange(0, 256)
                out.append('%%%02X' % b)
            else:
                out.append(r.choice(INPROC_SAFE_CHARS))
        return ''.join(out)[:length]
    strategies.append(s_pct)

    # Path-like segments
    def s_path():
        segs = []
        remaining = length
        while remaining > 0:
            seg_len = r.randint(1, max(1, min(8, remaining)))
            seg = ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(seg_len))
            segs.append(seg)
            remaining = length - sum(len(s) for s in segs) - min(1, remaining)
        s = '/'.join(segs)
        return s[:length]
    strategies.append(s_path)

    # Numeric-heavy (to emulate ports or ids in name)
    def s_numeric():
        digits = ''.join(r.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(max(1, length - 3)))
        prefix = r.choice(['id', 'grp', 'n', 'x'])
        s = (prefix + digits)[:length]
        if not s:
            s = '0'
        return s
    strategies.append(s_numeric)

    # Repeated character edge cases
    def s_repeat():
        ch = r.choice('aA0-_:.')
        return ch * length
    strategies.append(s_repeat)

    maker = r.choice(strategies)
    name = maker()
    # Ensure non-empty and avoid purely slash if weird generation; sanitize a bit
    if not name:
        name = 'x'
    # Trim to 32 chars maximum as stub will
    return name[:32]

def _build_dataset(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Curated list of interesting names
    dataset = [
        'a',
        'A',
        '0',
        'x' * 32,
        'with-dash_and.underscore',
        'seg/seg2/seg3',
        'name:with:colons',
        'plus+signs',
        'percent%2Fslash',
        'dots......',
        'UPPERlower123',
        'edge31chars_' + 'z' * 19,  # ensures > 31 after trim
    ]
    # Add several randomized entries
    for _ in range(20):
        dataset.append(_make_inproc_name(r))
    # Deduplicate preserving order
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for s in dataset:
        if s and s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            out.append(s)
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    names = _build_dataset(r)
    # Choose one name; the stub prepends inproc:// internally, but FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
    # receives only the name part per stub. It must be non-empty.
    name = r.choice(names)
    # Return as bytes; ensure <= 4096
    b = name.encode('utf-8')
    if len(b) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        b = b[:MAX_TOTAL_BYTES]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for ZeroMQ capability strings for zmq_has(capability)
# Any non-empty string is valid; recognized capabilities return non-zero.
# We bias toward known/common capability names, plus a variety of other
# plausible tokens to exercise different code paths, lengths, and charsets.

KNOWN_CAPABILITIES: List[str] = [
    # Common, widely known
    "curve",            # CURVE security
    "gssapi",           # GSSAPI mechanism
    "plain",            # PLAIN mechanism
    "ipc",              # ipc transport
    "tcp",              # tcp transport
    "pgm",              # PGM/EPGM multicast
    "vmci",             # VMware VMCI transport
    "norm",             # NORM transport
    "ws",               # WebSocket transport
    "wss",              # Secure WebSocket transport
    "draft",            # Draft APIs enabled
    "monitor",          # Socket monitoring
    "socks",            # SOCKS proxy support
    # Socket types / groups related (some implementations expose these as caps)
    "radio",
    "dish",
    "server",
    "client",
    "stream",
    "router",
    "dealer",
    # Features/options
    "ipc_thread_safe",
    "ipc_file_permissions",
    "msg_t_size_64",    # hypothetical size/build flags
]

# Additional interesting strings: extremes, unicode, punctuation, env-like, etc.
INTERESTING_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "0",                 # minimal digit
    "1",
    "ZMQ",              # uppercase token
    "capability",       # generic
    "CURVE",            # uppercase known
    "Curve",            # mixed case
    "inproc",           # inproc transport often always available
    "tipc",             # sometimes present
    "udp",              # not a zmq transport (should likely return 0)
    "\u2603",           # unicode snowman
    "\u00E9",           # accented char
    "feature.enable",   # dot
    "feature-enable",   # dash
    "feature_enable",   # underscore
    "x",                # single ASCII letter
    "longcapabilitynamewithnumbers1234567890",
    "Z85",
    "sodium",
    "libsodium",
    "eventfd",
    "epoll",
    "kqueue",
    "poll",
    "select",
]

# Allowed characters for random tokens
ALPHA = string.ascii_letters
ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
SYMS = "-_.:/+"
UNICODE_EXTRAS = [
    "π", "ß", "ø", "Ł", "Ж", "你", "好", "🙂"
]


def _rand_weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weight: float) -> str:
    # with probability weight, pick from items; else generate random token
    if rng.random() < weight:
        return rng.choice(items)
    return ""


def _random_token(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a token from segments to cover diverse cases while remaining printable
    parts: List[str] = []

    # Optionally add a known capability segment
    known = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, KNOWN_CAPABILITIES, 0.55)
    if known:
        parts.append(known)

    # Optionally add an interesting literal
    interesting = _rand_weighted_choice(rng, INTERESTING_STRINGS, 0.35)
    if interesting and interesting not in parts:
        parts.append(interesting)

    # Random alnum segment
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        n = rng.randint(1, 20)
        parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM) for _ in range(n)))

    # Random symbol separators
    if len(parts) > 1 and rng.random() < 0.7:
        sep = rng.choice(SYMS)
        token = sep.join(parts)
    else:
        token = ''.join(parts)

    # Possibly add unicode extras
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        token += rng.choice(UNICODE_EXTRAS)

    # If empty (all branches skipped), create a minimal non-empty token
    if not token:
        token = rng.choice(KNOWN_CAPABILITIES + INTERESTING_STRINGS)

    # Trim to reasonable length
    if len(token) > 256:
        token = token[:256]

    return token


def _make_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # For FUZZ_PARAM_STR used once, we return a single capability string
    # Optionally, we can package multiple candidates separated by NUL or newline,
    # but the stub expects a single std::string, so we return one.

    # Bias choices so we often hit real capabilities and sometimes unknown ones
    choice_pool: List[str] = []
    # Include known capabilities several times to increase selection chance
    for _ in range(3):
        choice_pool.extend(KNOWN_CAPABILITIES)
    choice_pool.extend(INTERESTING_STRINGS)

    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        cap = rng.choice(choice_pool)
    else:
        cap = _random_token(rng)

    # Ensure non-empty
    if not cap:
        cap = "curve"

    # Encode to UTF-8 bytes
    data = cap.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _make_payload(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Z85 character set per ZeroMQ ("0123456789" + ASCII letters and symbols excluding easily confused ones)
Z85_ALPHABET = (
    "0123456789"
    "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"
    ".-:+=^!/*?&<>()[]{}@%$#"
)

# Precompute a mapping for quick weighted generation if needed
Z85_CHARS: List[str] = list(Z85_ALPHABET)

# Some interesting 4-byte binary patterns and their Z85 encodings are non-trivial to compute here
# Instead, we will directly generate Z85 text ensuring it is valid length and uses valid alphabet.
# This aligns with the fuzzer stub which only requires txt.size() to be multiple of 5 and chars to be any text.

SPECIAL_GROUPS = [
    # All zero-like digit chars
    "00000",
    # Repetitions of edge chars in alphabet
    Z85_ALPHABET[0] * 5,                      # lowest value char
    Z85_ALPHABET[-1] * 5,                     # highest value char
    # Mixed punctuation-heavy group
    ".-:+=",
    # Brackets mixture
    "[]{}()",
]

def _rand_groups(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Fuzzer chooses groups in [1,8]. Bias toward boundaries and some middle values.
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8]
    return rng.choice(choices)

def _random_z85_group(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Occasionally pick a special group to exercise edge patterns
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        return rng.choice(SPECIAL_GROUPS)[:5]
    return ''.join(rng.choice(Z85_CHARS) for _ in range(5))

def _build_z85_text(rng: random.Random, groups: int) -> str:
    # Construct exactly groups*5 characters from valid alphabet
    parts: List[str] = []
    for i in range(groups):
        parts.append(_random_z85_group(rng))
    txt = ''.join(parts)
    # Ensure exact length (safety)
    if len(txt) != groups * 5:
        txt = (txt + (Z85_CHARS[0] * (groups * 5)))[: groups * 5]
    return txt

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Produce an initial valid buffer for the zmq_z85_decode fuzzer stub.
    The stub:
      - Picks groups in [1,8]
      - Requires input text length == groups*5
      - Calls zmq_z85_decode(outbuf, txt.c_str()) with outbuf sized for up to 8 groups
    We generate a Z85 text string with valid alphabet and length multiple of 5.
    Returned bytes are the textual buffer the harness will use via FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    groups = _rand_groups(rng)

    txt = _build_z85_text(rng, groups)

    # Return as bytes (UTF-8 ASCII-safe)
    return txt.encode('ascii')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for Z85-encoded Curve secret keys (40 chars + NUL expected by C API).
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a candidate secret key string,
# then enforces length 40 by padding/truncation and passes it to zmq_curve_public.
# Our goal is to return bytes that, when used as the FUZZ_PARAM_STR source,
# often yield valid Z85 secret keys to exercise success paths, while also
# exploring edge/corner cases within valid constraints.

# Z85 alphabet as defined by ZeroMQ (RFC): 85 characters
Z85_ALPHABET = (
    "0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ.\-:+=^!/*?&<>()[]{}@%$#"
)

# Some interesting boundary patterns of 40-char Z85 strings that stay valid length-wise.
INTERESTING_PATTERNS: List[str] = [
    # All zeros (valid charset; not guaranteed to be valid key, but tests parsing)
    "0" * 40,
    # All max-ish char '#'
    "#" * 40,
    # Alternating low/high chars
    ("0#" * 20)[:40],
    # Repeating base pattern of 5 (Z85 works on 4-byte groups -> 5 chars); length 40 is multiple of 5
    ("01234" * 8)[:40],
    # Mixed groups to exercise decoder diversity
    ("abcdE" * 8)[:40],
    (".-:+=" * 8)[:40],
    ("^!/*?" * 8)[:40],
    ("&<>()" * 8)[:40],
    ("[]{}@" * 8)[:40],
    ("%$#01" * 8)[:40],
]


def _rand_z85_string(rnd: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rnd.choice(Z85_ALPHABET) for _ in range(length))


def _make_valid_secret_candidates(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    candidates: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Proper 40-char Z85 strings likely to pass basic validation
    for _ in range(6):
        candidates.append(_rand_z85_string(rnd, 40).encode("ascii"))

    # 2) Known interesting patterns (still valid length/charset)
    for pat in INTERESTING_PATTERNS:
        candidates.append(pat.encode("ascii"))

    # 3) Include NUL-terminated version to match typical C expectations
    # The stub copies exactly 40 bytes then appends NUL itself, but providing
    # NUL here can still exercise string handling in higher layers.
    candidates.append((_rand_z85_string(rnd, 40) + "\x00").encode("latin1"))

    # 4) Edge: shorter strings that the stub pads to 40 with 'a'
    for sz in (0, 1, 5, 7, 10, 20, 39):
        s = _rand_z85_string(rnd, sz)
        candidates.append(s.encode("ascii"))

    # 5) Longer strings that the stub truncates to 40
    for sz in (41, 45, 60, 80):
        s = _rand_z85_string(rnd, sz)
        candidates.append(s.encode("ascii"))

    # 6) Mixed-case variants with groups of 5 repeated to keep group boundaries
    base_groups = [
        "01234", ".-:+=", "^!/*?", "&<>()", "[]{}@", "%$#01", "abcDE", "XYZw0",
    ]
    grp = rnd.choice(base_groups)
    candidates.append((grp * 8).encode("ascii"))

    # Ensure sizes remain reasonable
    trimmed: List[bytes] = []
    for c in candidates:
        if len(c) > 4096:
            c = c[:4096]
        trimmed.append(c)
    return trimmed


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of valid/interesting candidate buffers. The target stub only
    # uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR once, so returning one candidate is sufficient.
    candidates = _make_valid_secret_candidates(rnd)

    # Bias selection toward exactly-40-length candidates to increase success rate
    exact_40 = [c for c in candidates if len(c) == 40]
    if exact_40 and rnd.random() < 0.7:
        return rnd.choice(exact_40)

    return rnd.choice(candidates)
